body:
Crypto markets opened June on a sour note with the total market cap shedding 1.81% to $2.54T as selling pressure continued from last week's broader risk-off sentiment. The Fear & Greed index remains stuck at 29, barely budging from yesterday's 28 reading, reflecting the cautious positioning that's dominated trading flows. Volume clocked in at a respectable $78.8B, suggesting this isn't panic selling but rather methodical profit-taking and position sizing ahead of what could be a volatile summer.

Bitcoin dropped 2.26% to $72,139, breaking below the psychologically important $72,000 level that had provided support through most of May. The decline accelerated after news broke that MicroStrategy unloaded BTC for the first time in 4 years, selling 32 bitcoin for $2.5M in late May. While the amount is negligible compared to their massive holdings, the symbolic shift spooked leveraged longs. Key support now sits at $70,500, with the next major floor around $68,200. A bounce back above $73,500 would signal the sellers are exhausted, but momentum remains firmly bearish with BTC dominance holding steady at 57.0%.

Ethereum showed relative strength, declining only 1.83% to $1,983.29 despite the broader crypto selloff, maintaining its position as the day's least-worst performer among major assets. SOL followed closely with a 2.18% drop to $80.83, while BNB got hit hardest among the top coins, falling 4.19% to $693.07. The ETH/BTC pair actually gained ground, suggesting some rotation into the second-largest crypto as traders position for potential Ethereum ETF flows later this summer. XRP, ADA, and DOT all posted similar 2.7-2.9% declines, showing the selloff was broad-based rather than concentrated in any particular sector.

The macro backdrop remains challenging with Bitcoin ETPs posting their largest 2026 outflow as crypto funds bled $1.67B according to fresh data. ECB officials continue jawboning about stablecoin risks, while geopolitical tensions simmer with Trump's latest Iran comments adding uncertainty. The cancellation of Cardano Summit 2026 after community pushback on Foundation funding highlights ongoing governance tensions in major protocols. Meanwhile, traditional finance continues its crypto push with Binance adding US stock trading and Coinbase launching rupee rails in India.

This week's key catalyst will be Friday's jobs report, which could determine whether the Fed stays hawkish or signals a more dovish pivot. Any surprise weakness in employment could spark a risk-on rally across crypto, while a hot number would likely extend the current correction. Watch for any additional MicroStrategy selling, as corporate treasury moves continue to drive sentiment. The $70,500 level on Bitcoin is critical - a break below opens the door to $65,000, while a bounce here could set up a relief rally back toward $75,000 by mid-June.
